1.3 New in 1.1

This edition covers diskproxy 0.3.0. Since the first edition, the previews plugin has learned to give preview JPEGs their camera metadata and to keep the ratings given to them, and a photo library and a camera card can be served at once:

  • Metadata splicing. A map entry metadata= names a DNG or an EXIF-only TIFF, and the JPEG is served with its camera, lens, exposure, serial number and GPS EXIF, and its XMP packet, without copying image data.
  • One merged EXIF segment. A JPEG that already has EXIF, such as a Lightroom preview, has it replaced by one rebuilt segment: the JPEG’s own tags describe its pixels and win, the metadata file supplies the camera, and the map’s orientation and capture time win over both. There is one XMP packet: the JPEG’s own, unless the metadata file has one.
  • A metadata store. Instead of one small file per photo, metadata_store names a single SQLite file of them, opened read-only and immutable. Map paths are compared in composed Unicode (NFC).
  • Pixel tags stay the preview’s. Color space, resolution and the other tags that describe pixels never come from a metadata file.
  • Dates exFAT cannot hold no longer stop the disk: they are shown as the nearest time it can hold, with a warning naming the file.
  • Ratings that last. Clearing a rating, label or flag is captured too, and captured ratings are served back in the JPEGs and the stand-in DNGs after a restart, so an app reading the files sees what was written (Capturing ratings).
  • Several views at once. Each config file has its own view, so a photo library and a camera card can be mounted side by side, each started and stopped with its own --config (Everyday use).
  • Whichever card is mounted. The card ingest no longer needs the card’s name: when the configured card isn’t mounted, diskproxy uses the one camera card that is (Setting up).
  • Every camera file gets the corrected time, videos and thumbnails included, and a card whose ingests span a daylight-saving change is covered as well as one that travelled (The problem).

Two libraries built this way are described under Two libraries.
